top3.title: *Depose: Luigi Mangione, the Right to Health, and the Unfinished American Revolution* Book Launch Tour
top3.venue: Wooden Shoe Books, 704 South St, Philadelphia, PA 19147
top3.why: A spokesperson for the anonymous collective behind Luigi Mangione's legal fund presents "Depose," a book arguing his case is really about the right to health care in America. Wooden Shoe is the natural room for this — anarchist bookstore meets explicitly political publishing (Ill Will Editions, distributed by MIT Press), out the next day. Free, South Street, easy walk from Point Breeze.

top3.title: Sugar
top3.venue: Union Transfer, 1026 Spring Garden St., Philadelphia, PA 19123
top3.why: Bob Mould's Sugar reunite to play Copper Blue, the 1992 NME Album of the Year that bridged Hüsker Dü's hardcore roots into melodic alt-rock — essential listening for anyone who traces post-hardcore's lineage. A genuinely rare reunion show at a venue built for it. Tuesday's second Philly night, same tour, is a fallback if this one's sold out by the time you look.

top3.venue: PhilaMOCA, 531 N. 12th St, Philadelphia, PA 19123

A rare chance to hear Lynch's formative work discussed by someone who was actually there.

top3.venue_address: 2500 State Rd. unit d, Bensalem, PA 19020
top3.selection_address: 2500 State Rd Unit D, Bensalem, PA 19020
top3.why: Algernon Cadwallader — the Philly band whose name is basically shorthand for the 2000s emo revival — play a just-announced memorial show for a late friend, with all proceeds going to Savage Sisters' harm-reduction work. Genuinely rare: this isn't a standing tour, it's a one-off benefit. It's in Bensalem (Bucks County), about 15 miles from Center City — worth the trip for this bill specifically.

top3.title: HISTORY HAUNTS THIS ALLEY: A Journey into the Past
top3.venue: Elfreth’s Alley Museum, 126 Elfreth's Alley, Philadelphia, PA 19106
top3.why: A guided immersive theatrical walk through Elfreth's Alley, meeting six real past residents — portrayed by local actors — spanning 260 years of working-class life on America's oldest continuously inhabited residential street. Revives the alley's own street-theater tradition from the 1930s–40s. Old City, $15.
